Hi Samira —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and next steps so your security team has the right context: 

- What we covered: end-to-end flow for inference, latency SLOs, dedicated vs hosted options, and token-level cost controls.
- Key asks from Kalpana: data residency, audit logs retention, and proof points for SOC 2 controls.
- Next steps (owner): I shared our compliance packet (Redwood_Security_Summary_2026.pdf) and a short mutual action plan (attached) to accelerate review (Vivek). Monica will stand up a technical deep-dive if your infra team wants to test a sample workload (Monica).

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Summary_2026.pdf (summary + attestation matrix), Redwood_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (recommended milestones + owners)

If helpful, I can condense the packet into a one‑page attestation summary for your procurement/legal team — know you mentioned they prefer short artifacts. Are you able to share a preferred reviewer and an expected timeline for review?

Happy to set a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through any questions.

Thanks —

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful and appreciated. I forwarded the packet to our security and legal leads (CC'd Ben). Two quick clarifications before they dig in: 

1) Can you confirm our minimum retention window options (30 / 90 / 365 days) and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM (S3/Splunk)?
2) Any PII handling guidance or recommended config to ensure no long-term storage of user prompt text in hosted mode?

If you can drop a 1‑page attestation (yes on SOC 2 scope, encryption at rest, TLS in transit, KMS support, audit log retention options) that would speed the review.

Appreciate it — will follow up after the security sync.

Best,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: demo + compliance packet for Redwood evaluation

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the questions — quick answers inline and attaching a single-page attestation as requested. 

1) Retention: configurable. We support 30/90/365 day policies out-of-the-box; we can also set a custom retention window for Dedicated deployments.
2) PII: Hosted mode has prompt redaction options and optional KV caching controls; for sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or our Private deployment. We include a recommended config in the attestation doc.

Attached: Redwood_Attestation_Page_2026.pdf (one-page attestation that hits the bullets you listed).

If security wants a short session to validate the SIEM export flow (S3 + CloudTrail + Splunk forwarder), Monica can run a targeted demo with network diagrams and sample export events. Monica — can you and I line up 30 minutes later this week?

Thanks,
Vivek

If timing has shifted, totally understand — could you share the new priority/timeline so we can align our resources? If helpful, I'm happy to offer a short executive summary call (10–15 min) with KarThik to unblock procurement.

Hi Vivek — apologies for the slow reply. We ran through the packet with infra/security this morning. Overall it looks good — the attestation page was really helpful. A couple of asks before we can greenlight a pilot: 

- Can you provide an export example (sample CloudTrail + S3 object metadata) so our SIEM owner can test ingestion?
- We need a short signed attestation (PDF) on letterhead for procurement (Ben will handle the format).
- One more question around encryption keys: does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted deployments or only for Private?

If you can get the export example and the signed attestation to Ben by EOD Thursday, we should be able to move to procurement and scope a 4‑week pilot. Would appreciate a 20-min call Thursday to confirm details — Ben and I are free 3:00–4:30pm PT.

Thanks —
Samira
